title: Unit – 4 : Session – 10 : SLO – 2  |  Pipelining Performance — Fill in the Blanks
sections: 1. throughput — the primary pipelining metric, measured in instructions per cycle (IPC).
2. Pipeline stall — the pipeline pauses when dependencies cannot be resolved in time.
3. depth (number of stages) — ideal speedup equals the number of pipeline stages under perfect conditions.
4. Structural — hazards where multiple instructions need the same hardware resource.
5. Pipeline depth (ideal speedup) — Speedup = Pipeline depth / (1 + pipeline stall cycles per instruction).
6. Operand (result) — forwarding/bypassing reduces data hazards without waiting for register write-back.
7. Execute (EX) — branch conditions and target addresses are typically resolved in the execute stage.
8. Deep pipelines improve clock rate (throughput) but increase hazard/branch (stall) penalties.
9. Instruction-level — ILP lets multiple instructions execute in parallel within a single pipeline.
10. CPI — cycles per instruction, the average clock cycles each instruction needs.
